Update Desktop Graphics with Net.0 from Graphic Net

Adopting Net.0 for large-scale graphics production starts at the desk, and Graphic Net has strong opinions about what belongs on it. This blueprint lays out the hardware specs, the driver stack, and the rollout checklist the platform team recommends before a studio flips the switch.

The hardware guidance is tiered rather than one-size-fits-all. Template and production seats run comfortably on current mid-range GPUs with 32 GB of system memory, while seats driving real-time preview or the personalization engine warrant workstation-class cards and fast NVMe scratch space. The spec sheet marks which requirements are hard floors and which are comfort upgrades, which keeps procurement honest.

The driver stack is where most support tickets are born, so Net.0 ships with a certified matrix: GPU driver versions, color management components, and OS patch levels tested together as a set. Graphic Net's tooling pins the whole matrix and blocks partial upgrades, because a lone driver update that breaks color-managed export is the classic failure mode the certification exists to prevent.

The rollout checklist stages the migration in four passes: image a pilot pod and run it on real work for two weeks, calibrate displays against the new color pipeline, migrate shared asset caches during a maintenance window, and only then schedule the remaining seats in waves. Each pass has an explicit rollback point, and the checklist insists the pilot pod includes a skeptic.

Studios that follow the blueprint report the actual cutover as an anticlimax, which is the point. The drama belongs in the work, not in the workstation.
